# dsh-cron-jobs
Scheduled jobs for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): shell commands, agent prompts, or both.
DSH's built-in Schedule delivers a prompt to an agent session, so every tick starts a model turn. Th
at is wasteful for jobs that are only a script, or for a check that usually finds nothing. This plug
in runs jobs inside the DSH Host process, so they start and stop with DSH:

- A **command job** runs a shell command and never touches a model.
- A **gated job** runs its comma

nd first and wakes an agent only when the output says there is something to do.
- An **agent job** h
as no command: every run sends its prompt to an agent, like a scheduled task.
A job's result can be **delivered**: the woken agent's final answer, or a command's output and failu
res, is handed to another plugin that sends it on, such as a chat bot. This plugin knows no channel
itself; any plugin that provides a small `send` method can be one (see Result delivery).
Jobs run on cron expressions, RFC 5545 RRULE schedules, or once at a given time. They come from the
plugin config, or an agent creates them from a conversation with the plugin's tools ("remind me here
tomorrow at 9", "check this every Monday until January"). A **Cron tasks** page in the Web GUI show
s every job and its recent runs, and lets you run a job now, pause it, or delete one an agent create
every job and its recent runs, and lets you run a job now, pause it, or delete one an agent created.
## Install
Install it into the `web` profile straight from GitHub:

Then restart `dsh web` (or enable it on the Plugins page). To work on it locally instead, clone the
repository, install its dependencies, and install the directory as a bundle:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then ask the agent to install it, or call the plugin manager yourself:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The bundle adds two rows: `cron-jobs`, the scheduler, and `cron-jobs-tools`, which gives every agent
the tools described in Jobs created from a conversation. To give the tools to one agent preset only
, disable the `cron-jobs-tools` row and mount `dsh-cron-jobs/tools` in that preset instead.
Built and tested against DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 (`engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`). Commands run wit
h `bash -c`, or `sh -c` when bash is missing, so the Host needs a POSIX shell. The plugin needs DSH'
s storage domain service (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain`, part of every standard DSH composition)
for run history and pause state.
## Configure
Config jobs live in the config of the `cron-jobs` row. Add an override to your profile's `cordis.pat
ch.yml` (or edit the row on the plugin's settings page). An override replaces the whole `config`, so
list every job in it.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Meaning |

| `name` | Job name, used in logs and session titles. Must be unique. |
| `cron` | Cron expression:
5 fields, or 6 with seconds first. Parsed by croner, which handles daylight-saving changes like Vixi
e cron: a fixed time skipped by a spring forward runs at the first valid time after the gap, a fixed
time repeated by a fall back runs once, and patterns with several hours, minutes or seconds run on

both repeated occurrences. Set exactly one of `cron`, `rrule` and `at`. |
| `rrule` | RFC 5545 sched
ule: a `DTSTART` line and an `RRULE` line. The time zone comes from `DTSTART` (`TZID=...`, or `Z` fo

r UTC). See Schedules. |
| `at` | Run once at this time: ISO 8601 with an offset, or a local date-ti

me read in `timeZone`. |
| `timeZone` | IANA time zone for the cron expression or an `at` without of

fset. The Host's zone when empty. |
| `command` | Shell command line. Leave it out for an agent job.

|
| `cwd` | Working directory of the command. The Host process directory when empty. |
| `timeoutSe
conds` | Stop the command (and everything it started) after this long. Default 3600; `0` means no li

mit. |
| `enabled` | `false` keeps the job in the config without scheduling it. Default `true`. |
|
`deliver` | Where the job's result is sent: `{ via: <service name>, to: <address> }`, or `false` for
nothing. Unset: the row's `deliver`, except for jobs with `agent.sessionId`, which send nothing. Se

e Result delivery. |
| `agent.prompt` | With a command, makes the job a gated job; without one, an a

gent job. The prompt sent to the session. |
| `agent.sessionId` | Send the prompt into this existing

session instead of opening a new one. Such a session is never auto-archived. |
| `agent.preset` | A

gent preset of the new session. The Host default when empty. |
[该节后续省略]
## How runs work
- One run of a job at a time: if a tick arrives while the previous run is still going, the tick is s

kipped and logged.
- Start, exit status, duration and a short tail of stdout and stderr go to the DS

H log under `cron-jobs`. Sending the result anywhere else is what Result delivery is for.
- Set `run
Log` (next to `jobs`) to a file path to also keep that record as JSON Lines: one `start` line per ru
n, one `end` line with `status`, `outcome`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`, the output tails and the deliv
ery state, a `delivery` line when a woken agent's answer has been delivered (or not), a `skipped` li
ne for a skipped tick, an `overdue` line (with `dueAt` and `lateMs`) when a tick did not start on ti
me and the watchdog ran it late, and `scheduler-start` / `scheduler-stop` lines (with `job: null`) w
hen the scheduler starts or stops, so a gap in the log can be told apart from a lost tick. A `start`
with no `end` means DSH stopped during the run. The file is only appended to; rotate it yourself if

it grows.
- Ticks of config jobs missed while DSH is down are not caught up; the next tick runs nor
mally. While DSH runs, a watchdog checks every minute that each job's next run is not more than a mi
nute in the past; a tick whose timer was lost runs late instead of being missed. (Jobs created from

a conversation catch up once, see below.)
- Unloading the plugin (stopping DSH or changing its confi
g) stops the timers and terminates running commands.
